title: Waithe Lancaster Mid-Air Collision Memorial

external_narratives.summary: Registry entry for the Waithe memorial to four 100 Squadron Lancaster crews. A black polished marble tablet records the details of crews from Lancaster JB678 and three other aircraft lost from RAF Grimsby (Waltham) during Black Thursday, 16/17 December 1943.
external_narratives.key_details: Combined memorial on the A16 Louth Road at Holton Le Clay commemorates four 100 Squadron Lancaster crews. JB678 collided with JB674 on return from the Berlin raid. Part of the Black Thursday disaster.

external_narratives.summary: Comprehensive account of Black Thursday, 16 December 1943, when almost 300 RAF airmen died. Lancaster JB678 was among 100 Squadron's losses, involved in a mid-air collision with JB674 while returning to fog-bound RAF Grimsby after the Berlin raid.
external_narratives.key_details: 100 Squadron lost their CO, W/C David Holford DSO DFC, plus multiple other aircraft that night. JB678 and JB674 collided at 00:40 on the 17th while circling the fog-bound airfield waiting to land.
external_narratives.link_description: Explore detailed account of Black Thursday tragedy and Lancaster JB678's involvement in this poignant memorial link.

external_narratives.summary: Registry entry for the Waithe combined memorial commemorating four 100 Squadron Lancaster crews lost on Black Thursday. Lancaster JB674, piloted by F/Sgt Allen Kevis, collided with Lancaster JB678 at 00:40 on 17 December 1943 while both aircraft circled the fog-bound airfield.
external_narratives.key_details: JB674 is one of four 100 Squadron aircraft commemorated on the combined black marble memorial tablet. The collision occurred during the return from the Berlin raid in dense fog.
external_narratives.link_description: The poignant story of four 100 Squadron Lancaster crews tragically lost in World War II.

external_narratives.summary: Account of Black Thursday documenting the catastrophic losses at fog-bound airfields. Lancaster JB674 from 100 Squadron collided mid-air with JB678 after both had survived the Berlin raid, only to die in English fog waiting to land.
external_narratives.key_details: The collision of JB674 and JB678 was one of the cruelest ironies of Black Thursday — crews surviving the most dangerous target in Germany only to die within sight of their home airfield.
external_narratives.link_description: Explore detailed account of Black Thursday's tragic aircraft collisions amidst fog-bound RAF airfields.

external_narratives.summary: 100 Squadron history page documenting the unit's WW2 formation, operations, and losses. Includes the Black Thursday losses among the squadron's operational record from RAF Grimsby (Waltham).
external_narratives.key_details: 100 Squadron operated from RAF Grimsby (also known as Waltham) as part of 1 Group, Bomber Command. The squadron suffered disproportionately heavy losses on 16/17 December 1943.
external_narratives.link_description: Explore Lancaster Memorial: Discover WWII 100 Squadron's history, including formation, operations, and significant losses at RAF Grimsby.

external_narratives.summary: Biographical article on Wing Commander David William Holford DSO DFC (21 February 1921 - 17 December 1943), who was the youngest bomber squadron commanding officer in RAF history when he took command of 100 Squadron at age 21 in February 1943.
external_narratives.key_details: Holford was 22 when killed. He had already completed two full tours of operations. Appointed CO of 100 Squadron at Waltham on 21 November 1943. Crashed Lancaster JB560 in thick fog near Kelstern after the Black Thursday Berlin raid.
external_narratives.link_description: Biographical details of Wing Commander David William Holford, RAF's youngest bomber squadron commander.

external_narratives.summary: International Bomber Command Centre loss record for Lancaster JB560 and W/C Holford. Documents the operational details and crew information for this Black Thursday loss.
external_narratives.key_details: IBCC loss record reference 111010. Lancaster JB560 was the aircraft carrying the 100 Squadron commanding officer on the Berlin raid of 16/17 December 1943.
external_narratives.link_description: Detailed records of Lancaster JB560's tragic "Black Thursday" crash, including crew losses and operational history from IBCC Digital Archive.

external_narratives.summary: The Waithe combined memorial commemorates W/C Holford's crew alongside three other 100 Squadron Lancaster crews lost on Black Thursday. The memorial is a black polished marble tablet on the A16 Louth Road.
external_narratives.key_details: Holford's loss was devastating for 100 Squadron — losing their CO alongside multiple other crews in a single night. Two crew members survived the crash of JB560.
external_narratives.link_description: The poignant Waithe (4) Lancaster Memorial honoring fallen crew members of Black Thursday.

external_narratives.summary: RAF Commands war dead database entry for Wing Commander D.W. Holford (service number 41704), recording his death on 17 December 1943 while serving with 100 Squadron.
external_narratives.key_details: Service number 41704. Holford held both the DSO and DFC. His death at 22 made him one of the youngest wing commanders to be killed in Bomber Command.

narrative: Lancaster JB678 of 100 Squadron, based at RAF Grimsby, was returning from a major raid on Berlin on the night of 16/17 December 1943, part of a force of 483 Lancasters and 15 Mosquitos. The aircraft came down at Waithe, Lincolnshire, close to its home airfield, amid fog-bound conditions that caused multiple collisions among returning aircraft that night. Two crew members were killed: Pilot Officer Robert Herbert Chapman and Wing Commander David William Holford, who was 22 years old. The remaining eight crew members survived.
community_connection: There are memorials dedicated to him at Waithe Farm, Waithe, Lincolnshire and off the A16, Holton le Clay, Lincolnshire.
